gaps: P0: none. P5: none (all Mittelholzer aerials #20–#23 are Koblenz in Aargau, Switzerland). P6: no good view of the center — #24 is a dusk HDR panorama from Metternich in which nothing is recognizable; #25 (Neuendorf) and #26 (Stolzenfels) are outlying districts; #27 is the Rhine gorge near Niederheimbach.
notes: #3 date: the Trier–Koblenz–Rothenburg plate is taken as vol. 1 (1572); Commons says ‘about 1570’ and the plate sits among vol. 1 German cities in the 1582 German edition (#4) — change to 1575 if it proves to be vol. 2. #1 is a colored crop of the same panel but has a fold through the middle. P1/P2 alternative: Merian’s bird’s-eye view (#7, Topographia of Mainz, Trier and Cologne, 1646; #5 is a crop of it) shows the Swedish siege of 1632 and would need event: true. P2 alternative: Jacobus Storck’s painting (#8, 1680–99, color), but it looks at Ehrenbreitstein and the Philippsburg palace from the Koblenz shore, with a possibly invented foreground. P3 alternative: Wittoff’s painting (#12, 1836) of the Electoral Palace and Ehrenbreitstein, color, wide. P4: the 1860s stereo cards (#14–#16) are by Adolphe Braun, not Braun and Hogenberg; #17 is Stolzenfels castle and #19 is Kobern on the Moselle, not Koblenz.
